examples.en: My arm feels itchy, maybe from a mosquito bite.

examples.ko: 목이 간질간질하면 감기가 올 것 같아요.
examples.en: When my throat tickles, it feels like a cold is coming.
My back is itchy but I can't reach it.
My head tickles as if a bug were crawling on it.
The tip of my nose tickled, and then I sneezed.
The child laughs and says the soles of their feet tickle.

explain: '가렵다'는 긁고 싶은 느낌이고, '간지럽다'는 살짝 건드려서 웃음이 나올 수 있는 느낌인데, '간질간질'은 후자 쪽의 가벼운 느낌을 나타내요. 목이나 코가 근질거릴 때도 써요. 말하고 싶은 마음을 비유할 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 비밀을 알고 있는데 말을 못 해서 입이 간질간질해요.
phrases.en: I know a secret but can't tell anyone, so I'm itching to say it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하고 싶은 마음을 참기 힘들 때 써요. 입이 실제로 간지러운 게 아니라 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is hard to hold back the urge to say something. The mouth is not literally itchy; it is a figure of speech.

explain_en: '가렵다' is an itch you want to scratch, while '간지럽다' is a light tickling feeling that can make you laugh, and '간질간질' expresses that lighter feeling. It is also used when your throat or nose tickles. It can also be used figuratively for an urge to speak.

examples.ko: 곁길을 따라 걸으니 작은 시장이 나왔어요.
examples.en: I walked along the side street and came to a small market.

examples.ko: 큰길 옆 곁길에 조용한 카페가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a quiet cafe on the side street next to the main road.

examples.ko: 이 곁길은 차가 거의 안 다녀서 산책하기 좋아요.
examples.en: Hardly any cars use this side road, so it's good for walks.

examples.ko: 이야기가 자꾸 곁길로 새서 본론을 못 말했어요.
examples.en: The conversation kept drifting off topic, so I couldn't get to the main point.

examples.ko: 아이는 학교가 끝나면 곁길로 빠지지 않고 집에 와요.
examples.en: After school, the child comes straight home without wandering off.

examples.ko: 곁길도 많아서 처음 오는 사람은 헷갈려요.
examples.en: There are many side roads too, so first-timers get confused.

explain: 큰길에서 갈라져 나온 작은 길이에요. 비유로 '본래 가려던 방향이나 주제에서 벗어난 것'에도 써서 '곁길로 새다', '곁길로 빠지다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: go off on a tangent
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이나 행동이 원래 주제나 목적에서 벗어날 때 써요. 때로는 옳지 않은 방향으로 빠진다는 뜻도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when speech or actions drift away from the original topic or goal. It can also suggest going down the wrong path.

explain_en: It means a small road branching off a main road. It is also used figuratively for straying from the intended direction or topic, as in '곁길로 새다' and '곁길로 빠지다'.

examples.ko: 제목은 고딕체를 쓰는 게 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: It looks nice to use a Gothic font for the title.

examples.ko: 보고서 본문은 고딕체 대신 명조체로 바꿨어요.
examples.en: I changed the report body from Gothic to Myeongjo font.

examples.ko: 이 글꼴은 고딕체라서 화면에서 읽기 쉬워요.
examples.en: This font is Gothic, so it's easy to read on screen.

examples.ko: 발표 자료에는 굵은 고딕체가 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: A bold Gothic font suits presentation slides well.

examples.ko: 고딕체로 쓰인 간판이 멀리서도 잘 보여요.
examples.en: The sign written in a Gothic font is easy to see even from far away.

examples.ko: 고딕체와 명조체는 글자 끝 모양이 달라요.
examples.en: Gothic and Myeongjo fonts differ in the shape of the letter ends.

explain: 획의 굵기가 비슷하고 끝에 삐침이 없는 글꼴이에요. 삐침이 있는 '명조체'와 짝으로 자주 말해요. 제목이나 화면용 글자에 많이 쓰고, 컴퓨터 글꼴 이름에도 '고딕'이 자주 들어가요.

phrases.en: I wrote the title in Gothic type.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글꼴을 정해서 쓸 때 '-로'를 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -로 to say which font you use for writing.

phrases.en: I changed the title to bold Gothic type.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자를 두껍게 해서 눈에 띄게 할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when making the text thick so it stands out.

phrases.example: 본문은 명조체로 쓰고 제목은 고딕체로 써요.
phrases.en: I use Myeongjo type for the body text and Gothic type for the title.
phrases.nuance_ko: 획 끝에 삐침이 있는 글꼴로, '고딕체'와 짝으로 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typeface with serifs at the stroke ends, often mentioned as a pair with 고딕체.

explain_en: It is a typeface with fairly even stroke thickness and no flicks at the ends of strokes. It is often paired with '명조체', which has those flicks. It is common for titles and on-screen text, and '고딕' often appears in computer font names.

examples.en: The shirt got all crumpled inside the bag.
I folded the paper in a crumpled way and put it in my pocket.
I finally found the crumpled receipt.
The child crumpled up the letter and threw it.

examples.ko: 바지가 구깃구깃 주름져서 입고 나갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: The pants are so wrinkled that I can't go out in them.

examples.ko: 옷을 구깃구깃 넣었더니 꺼낼 때 다 구겨져 있어요.
examples.en: I stuffed the clothes in carelessly, so they are all wrinkled when I take them out.

explain: 종이나 옷이 여기저기 마구 구겨진 모습을 나타내요. '구기다', '구겨지다'와 같이 쓰이고, 상태를 말할 때는 '구깃구깃한 옷'처럼 '구깃구깃하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I tried smoothing out the crumpled paper with my hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구깃구깃하다'로 바꿔서 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Changed to 구깃구깃하다 to describe a noun.

phrases.en: The book got soaked in the rain and wrinkled all over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저절로 여기저기 구겨지는 변화에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something gets wrinkled all over by itself.

phrases.en: I was angry, so I crumpled the letter up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 일부러 마구 구기는 동작에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone deliberately crumples something.

explain_en: It describes paper or clothes crumpled all over in a messy way. It goes with '구기다' and '구겨지다'. To describe a state, use '구깃구깃하다', as in '구깃구깃한 옷'.

examples.ko: 꼬질꼬질 때가 낀 운동화를 오늘 빨았어요.
examples.en: I washed my grubby, dirt-caked sneakers today.
The child came in all grubby and covered in dirt.
The old teddy bear has gotten all grubby.

examples.ko: 꼬질꼬질 때가 탄 이불을 주말에 빨 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to wash the grimy blanket this weekend.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 꼬질꼬질 낡은 옷을 입고 있었어요.
examples.en: The kid was wearing dirty, worn-out clothes.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 뛰어놀았더니 얼굴이 꼬질꼬질 지저분해요.
examples.en: After running around all day, my face is grimy and messy.

explain: 오래 씻거나 빨지 않아 때가 타서 꾀죄죄한 모습에 써요. 사람, 옷, 인형 모두에 쓸 수 있지만 사람에게 직접 말하면 기분이 나쁠 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I haven't washed for days, so my hair is grubby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사에 '-하다'가 붙은 형용사로, 때가 탄 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form, describing a dirty, grimy state.

phrases.en: Wash grubby clothes before you wear them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-한'을 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-한' to modify the noun that follows.

phrases.en: It's an old, worn-out piece of clothing, so it looks scruffy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고, 지저분하고 초라해 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning; used when something looks dirty and shabby.

explain_en: It describes something shabby and grimy because it hasn't been washed for a long time. You can use it for people, clothes and toys, but saying it directly to a person can offend them.

examples.en: This book is so old that it's falling apart.
I'm embarrassed to go out wearing tattered clothes.
Your shoes have become tattered, so buy a new pair.
The rag that I've used for so long is in shreds.
The bag is tattered, but I still treasure it.
After working all night, I feel completely worn to shreds.

explain: 낡고 찢어져서 여기저기 늘어진 상태를 말해요. 사람이 너무 지쳤을 때 '몸이 너덜너덜해졌다'처럼 비유로도 써요.

phrases.en: The album I've looked at for years has become tattered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점점 낡아 가는 과정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the gradual process of wearing out.

phrases.example: 너덜너덜한 가방이지만 정이 들어서 못 버리겠어요.
phrases.en: It's a tattered bag, but I've grown attached to it and can't throw it away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 낡은 모습을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to describe its worn look.

phrases.en: Overtime keeps piling up, so my body is worn to shreds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 지쳤을 때 비유로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative expression for being completely exhausted.

explain_en: It describes something so worn and torn that it hangs in pieces. It is also used figuratively for exhaustion, as in '몸이 너덜너덜해졌다'.

examples.en: I finished the wooden chair until it was smooth.

examples.ko: 발표 전에 원고를 한 번 더 다듬질해 보세요.
examples.en: Try polishing the script once more before the presentation.
I'm putting the finishing touches on the painting now.

examples.ko: 거친 면을 사포로 다듬질하면 훨씬 부드러워져요.
examples.en: If you finish the rough surface with sandpaper, it becomes much smoother.

examples.ko: 글을 다듬질하고 나니 문장이 훨씬 자연스러워요.
examples.en: After polishing the text, the sentences read much more naturally.

examples.ko: 조각을 다듬질할 때는 천천히 해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to go slowly when you finish a sculpture.

explain: 물건이나 글을 마지막으로 매만져 완성도를 높일 때 써요. 글을 고칠 때는 '다듬다'가 더 일상적이고, '다듬질하다'는 목공이나 공예 같은 마무리 작업에 잘 어울려요. 일반적으로 겉을 '손질하다'라고 하는 것보다 마지막 단계라는 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.example: 글을 한 번 더 다듬어 보세요.
phrases.en: Please polish your writing one more time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 널리 쓰는 말이고 글이나 머리 모양에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday word, also used for writing or hairstyles.

phrases.en: I finished the last bit of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 끝내는 단계를 넓게 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broad word for the final stage of finishing a task.

phrases.en: I finished the final touches on the wooden box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공예나 목공의 마지막 손질을 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits the final touches in woodwork or crafts.

explain_en: It is used when you give something a final touch to raise its quality, whether an object or a text. For editing writing, '다듬다' is more everyday, while '다듬질하다' fits finishing work like woodworking and crafts. Compared with the general '손질하다', it feels more like the last stage.

en: old year; the year just ended

examples.en: It is the night we see off the old year and welcome the new one.

examples.ko: 묵은해의 걱정은 다 잊고 새로 시작해요.
examples.en: Let's forget the worries of the old year and start fresh.
At the end of the year, I look back on what happened in the past year.
A bell rings between the old year and the new year.

examples.ko: 묵은해가 가는 게 아쉬워서 친구들과 밤새 이야기했어요.
examples.en: I was sad to see the old year go, so I talked with friends all night.
The old year is gone and the new year has come.

explain: '지난해'는 그냥 지나간 해를 말하고, '묵은해'는 새해를 맞이하며 보내는 해라는 느낌이 있어요. 연말연시에 주로 쓰고, 짝말은 '새해'예요.

phrases.en: We saw off the old year with our family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연말에 한 해를 마무리할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when wrapping up the year at its end.
phrases.en_equiv: to see off the old year

phrases.en: It's the time when the old year turns into the new year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새해'와 짝으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with '새해'.
phrases.en_equiv: the old year and the new year

phrases.en: Last year I traveled a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새해 느낌 없이 그냥 지나간 해를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Just means last year, without the New Year feeling.

explain_en: '지난해' simply means the year that passed, while '묵은해' feels like the year you are seeing off as the new one arrives. It is mostly used around New Year, and its counterpart is '새해'.

examples.en: The boiled potatoes cooked until soft.
A ripe persimmon feels soft when you touch it.
I boiled it too long, so the noodles got mushy.

examples.ko: 이 푸딩은 너무 물렁물렁해서 모양이 안 잡혀요.
examples.en: This pudding is so mushy that it won't hold its shape.

examples.ko: 물렁물렁한 바나나는 빵을 만들 때 쓰면 좋아요.
examples.en: Mushy bananas are good to use when baking bread.
If a pear is mushy, it has gone bad inside.

explain: '물렁물렁하다'로 훨씬 자주 쓰고, 단단하지 않고 푹 눌리는 느낌이에요. '말랑말랑'은 기분 좋게 부드러운 느낌이고, '물렁물렁'은 너무 무른 느낌이 들 때가 많아요. 반대는 '단단하다'이고, 사람에게 '물렁하다'라고 하면 성격이 약하고 만만하다는 말로 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: This peach is too soft and mushy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훨씬 자주 쓰는 형용사 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form, which is used far more often.

phrases.en: I ate the soft persimmon with a spoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸미는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to describe a noun.

phrases.en: After I left it a long time, the tomato went mushy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단단하던 것이 변할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something firm changes and becomes soft.

explain_en: It is used far more often as '물렁물렁하다', and it describes something that is not firm and gives way when pressed. '말랑말랑' feels pleasantly soft, while '물렁물렁' often feels too soft. The opposite is '단단하다', and calling a person '물렁하다' can sound like they are weak or easy to push around.

examples.ko: 한국 전통 공연에서 부채춤을 처음 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the fan dance for the first time at a Korean traditional performance.
The fan dance goes well with colorful hanbok.
My friends performed the fan dance at the school festival.

examples.ko: 외국인 관광객이 부채춤 공연을 보고 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: Foreign tourists clapped after watching the fan dance performance.

examples.ko: 부채춤에서 부채가 꽃처럼 펼쳐지는 장면이 예뻤어요.
examples.en: The scene in the fan dance where the fans open like flowers was beautiful.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 부채춤을 배운 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I learned the fan dance when I was little.

explain: '부채춤을 추다'처럼 '추다'와 함께 써요. 한복을 입고 하는 공연에서 자주 볼 수 있어서 한국 문화를 소개할 때 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 무대에서 열 명이 함께 부채춤을 춰요.
phrases.en: Ten people dance the fan dance together on stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 춤을 직접 한다고 말할 때 '추다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '추다' to say someone performs the dance.

phrases.example: 외국 손님들에게 부채춤 공연을 보여 줬어요.
phrases.en: We showed a fan dance performance to the foreign guests.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공연이나 행사 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about shows or events.

phrases.example: 저는 한국 문화 수업에서 부채춤을 배워요.
phrases.en: I learn the fan dance in my Korean culture class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국 문화를 체험하거나 배울 때 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Good for talking about experiencing or learning Korean culture.

explain_en: It is used with '추다' (to dance), as in '부채춤을 추다'. You often see it in performances in hanbok, so it comes up a lot when introducing Korean culture.

examples.en: I got a doctor's note from the hospital and submitted it to my company.
You need a referral note to go to a large hospital.
Where do I get the doctor's note issued?

examples.ko: 소견서에 제 상태가 자세히 적혀 있었어요.
examples.en: My condition was written in detail in the note.

examples.ko: 소견서 한 장 때문에 병원을 두 번 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the hospital twice just for one doctor's note.
Can I apply for insurance with this note?

explain: 진단서가 병명을 공식적으로 증명하는 서류라면, 소견서는 의사의 의견을 적은 글이에요. 다른 병원으로 갈 때 받는 서류는 '진료의뢰서'라고도 해요. 보통 '소견서를 받다/떼다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I got a doctor's note from the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '받다'보다 서류를 직접 발급받는 느낌으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a feel of getting the document issued yourself, compared with '받다'.

phrases.en: The doctor wrote me a note.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의사가 서류를 작성해 주는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the doctor prepares the document for you.

phrases.en: I got a referral and went to a big hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 병원으로 갈 때 받는 소견서를 이렇게도 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another name for the note you get when moving to another hospital.

explain_en: If a 진단서 is an official document certifying a diagnosis, a 소견서 is a written statement of the doctor's opinion. A document for moving to another hospital is also called '진료의뢰서'. People usually say '소견서를 받다' or '소견서를 떼다'.

examples.en: I tried drawing notes on staff paper.
The teacher drew a staff on the blackboard.
The composer wrote a melody on the staff paper.
I didn't have staff paper, so I drew lines in my notebook.
I bought a new book of staff paper.
Try copying the song onto staff paper.

explain: '악보'와 달리 음표를 적기 전의 줄만 그어진 종이를 말해요. 음악 시간이나 작곡 이야기에서 나오고, 비유로 '오선지 위의 음악'처럼도 써요.

phrases.en: I wrote a melody on staff paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악을 만들거나 악보를 쓸 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when composing or writing music.

phrases.en: I bought a sheet of blank staff paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음표가 없는 줄만 있는 종이라는 뜻을 분명히 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear it is paper with only the lines and no notes.

phrases.example: 오선지 위의 음표가 춤추는 것 같아요.
phrases.en: The notes on the staff look like they are dancing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음표가 놓인 모습을 말하거나 비유로 쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for notes sitting on the staff, or figuratively.

explain_en: Unlike '악보' (sheet music), it refers to paper with just the five lines, before notes are written. It appears in music class or composing talk.

examples.ko: 아이의 자립심을 키우려면 혼자 해 보게 하세요.
examples.en: To build a child's independence, let them try things alone.
I moved out early, so I became more self-reliant.

examples.ko: 자립심 있는 청년이 되도록 가르치고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to teach them to become self-reliant young people.
Independence starts with small things.
I learned self-reliance by traveling alone.
After living alone, my sense of independence grew too.

explain: 남에게 기대지 않고 스스로 해 나가려는 마음이에요. '자립심을 기르다/키우다'처럼 많이 말하고, 아이 교육이나 독립 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I built up my independence by traveling alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '키우다'보다 조금 더 글 같은 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Slightly more formal-sounding than '키우다'.

phrases.en: I developed a sense of independence from living alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경험을 통해 자연스럽게 그런 마음이 생길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the feeling arises naturally from experience.

phrases.en: If you leave everything to your parents, you end up lacking independence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 하려는 마음이 약할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the will to do things on one's own is weak.

explain_en: It is the mind-set of trying to manage on your own without leaning on others. It is often said as '자립심을 기르다/키우다' and appears a lot in talk about raising children or becoming independent.

examples.ko: 사진을 찍을 때는 피사체와의 거리가 중요해요.
examples.en: When taking photos, the distance to the subject is important.

examples.ko: 이 카메라는 움직이는 피사체도 선명하게 찍어요.
examples.en: This camera captures even moving subjects clearly.

examples.ko: 피사체가 너무 어두워서 사진이 흐리게 나왔어요.
examples.en: The subject was too dark, so the photo came out blurry.

examples.ko: 그 사진작가는 평범한 사람들을 피사체로 삼아요.
examples.en: That photographer takes ordinary people as his subjects.
If you focus on the subject, the background gets blurred.

examples.ko: 아이들은 가만히 있지 않아서 찍기 쉬운 피사체가 아니에요.
examples.en: Kids don't stay still, so they aren't easy subjects to photograph.

explain: 사진이나 영상에서 찍히는 대상을 말하고, 사람·동물·풍경·물건 모두 해당돼요. 사진 이야기나 카메라 설명에서 주로 나오고, 사람을 가리켜 '모델'이라고 부르는 것과는 달라요.

phrases.en: I focused the camera on the subject.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사진을 찍을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase used when taking photos.

phrases.en: Moving subjects are hard to capture in photos.
phrases.nuance_ko: '움직이는'을 앞에 붙여 찍기 어려운 대상을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting '움직이는' in front describes a subject that is hard to shoot.

phrases.en: This lake is a good subject for photographers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사진으로 찍기 좋은 대상이나 장소를 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise something or somewhere that looks good in photos.

explain_en: It means whatever is being photographed or filmed, whether a person, animal, landscape or object. It mostly comes up in talk about photography and camera descriptions, and differs from calling a person a '모델' (model).

examples.en: We measured the salt content of the seawater.

examples.ko: 해수는 짜서 그냥 마실 수 없어요.
examples.en: Seawater is salty, so you can't just drink it.
The seawater around the beach is clear.
This plant turns seawater into fresh water.
The typhoon grew stronger because the seawater temperature was high.
Seawater contains a lot of salt.

explain: 일상에서는 '바닷물'이라고 하고, '해수'는 과학이나 뉴스에서 써요. 반대로 강이나 호수의 물은 '담수'나 '민물'이라고 해요. '해수욕'에도 이 글자가 들어 있어요.

phrases.en: Seawater is salty, so you can't drink it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해수'와 같은 뜻으로 일상 대화에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday word for the same thing as '해수'.

phrases.en: In summer, the seawater temperature rises.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학이나 뉴스에서 바닷물 온도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in science or news to talk about the sea's temperature.

phrases.en: I went swimming in the sea with my family on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닷물에서 수영하거나 노는 것을 말하고, 이 글자가 들어 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Swimming or playing in the sea, a word that contains this same character.

explain_en: In daily life people say '바닷물'; '해수' is for science and the news. Water from rivers and lakes is '담수' or '민물'. The same characters appear in '해수욕', swimming at the sea.

examples.en: This park is a good place to rest for office workers.

examples.ko: 집 근처에 조용한 휴식처가 생겨서 좋아요.
examples.en: I'm glad a quiet place to relax opened near my house.

examples.ko: 등산로 중간에 있는 휴식처에서 잠깐 쉬었어요.
examples.en: I rested for a while at the rest spot midway along the trail.

examples.ko: 저에게 카페는 바쁜 하루의 휴식처 같은 곳이에요.
examples.en: For me, a café is like a refuge in a busy day.

examples.ko: 아이들에게 편안한 휴식처를 만들어 주고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to make a comfortable resting place for the kids.

examples.ko: 여행이 끝나면 집이 가장 좋은 휴식처라는 생각이 들어요.
examples.en: After a trip, I feel that home is the best place to rest.

explain: 고속도로에서 쉬어 가는 곳은 '휴게소'라고 하고, '휴식처'는 쉴 수 있는 장소를 더 넓게 말해요. '마음의 휴식처'처럼 마음이 편해지는 사람이나 장소를 비유할 때도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: To me, my family is a place of rest for my heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편안함을 주는 사람이나 장소를 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for a person or place that brings comfort.

phrases.en: This cafe has become my place to rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곳이 쉬는 장소로 자리 잡았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a place has become somewhere you regularly go to relax.

phrases.en: There is a small rest area in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휴식처'와 비슷하지만 잠깐 앉아서 쉬는 작은 장소를 말할 때 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '휴식처', but more often a small spot to sit and rest briefly.

explain_en: A highway stop is called '휴게소', while '휴식처' refers more broadly to any place where you can rest. It is also used figuratively, as in '마음의 휴식처' (a place of mental refuge).
